normalized-residual.title: Normalized Model Residual
normalized-residual.meaning: Shows how many combined standard uncertainties separate an observation from the model's prediction.
normalized-residual.conditions: The uncertainties must be standard, independent, and approximately normally distributed; covariance is required when they are correlated.
normalized-residual.units: z: dimensionless; x and σ: the same SI units

uncertainty-propagation.title: Propagation of Independent Uncertainties
uncertainty-propagation.meaning: Estimates the standard uncertainty of a calculated quantity from the uncertainties of the input data.
uncertainty-propagation.conditions: Linearization is valid for small uncertainties; the input quantities are uncorrelated, otherwise covariance terms must be added.
uncertainty-propagation.units: σ_f: the SI unit of f; each term in the sum: the square of the unit of f

vector-dot-product.title: Dot Product of Vectors
vector-dot-product.plain: a · b = |a||b| cos θ = Σ_i a_i b_i
vector-dot-product.meaning: Relates the geometric angle between vectors to their components and isolates the longitudinal component.
vector-dot-product.conditions: The component-sum form is written in an orthonormal Euclidean basis.
vector-dot-product.units: the product of the SI units of quantities a and b

velocity-acceleration.title: Instantaneous Velocity and Acceleration
velocity-acceleration.meaning: Velocity gives the rate of change of position, while acceleration gives the rate of change of velocity.
velocity-acceleration.conditions: The trajectory must be differentiable with respect to time in the chosen frame of reference.
velocity-acceleration.units: r: m; v: m/s; a: m/s²

constant-acceleration-motion.title: Motion with Constant Acceleration
constant-acceleration-motion.plain: v(t) = v₀ + at; r(t) = r₀ + v₀t + at²/2
constant-acceleration-motion.meaning: Gives a body's velocity and position as functions of time when its acceleration remains constant.
constant-acceleration-motion.conditions: Acceleration is constant in both magnitude and direction throughout the interval considered; time is measured from the initial state.
constant-acceleration-motion.units: r: m; v: m/s; a: m/s²; t: s

newton-second-law.title: Newton's Second Law
newton-second-law.plain: ΣF = dp/dt; for constant mass, ΣF = ma
newton-second-law.meaning: The net external force determines the change in a body's momentum.
newton-second-law.conditions: An inertial frame and a material system of fixed composition; the ma form additionally requires constant mass and nonrelativistic motion. For an open system such as a rocket, momentum flux must be included separately.
newton-second-law.units: F: N; p: kg·m/s; m: kg; a: m/s²

dry-friction.title: Dry Friction
dry-friction.meaning: Static friction adjusts up to a limiting value, while kinetic friction points opposite to the relative velocity.
dry-friction.conditions: This is the empirical Coulomb–Amontons model for dry surfaces; the coefficients depend on the pair of materials and the condition of their surfaces.
dry-friction.units: F and N: N; μ_s and μ_k: dimensionless

work-energy-theorem.title: Work–Energy Theorem
work-energy-theorem.plain: W_net = ∫ F_net · dr = ΔK; K = mv²/2
work-energy-theorem.meaning: The work done by the net force equals the change in the body's kinetic energy.
work-energy-theorem.conditions: The expression K = mv²/2 is valid for a point particle of constant mass at nonrelativistic speeds.
work-energy-theorem.units: W and K: J; F: N; r: m

rotational-kinetic-energy.title: Rigid-Body Kinetic Energy and Rolling
rotational-kinetic-energy.plain: K = Mv_cm²/2 + I_cmω²/2; v_cm = ωR for rolling without slipping
rotational-kinetic-energy.meaning: Splits the kinetic energy of a rigid body in planar motion into translation of its center of mass and rotation about it; the no-slip condition relates the two speeds.
rotational-kinetic-energy.conditions: A perfectly rigid body undergoes planar motion, with a principal axis through its center of mass. The relation v_cm = ωR applies to a round body of radius R rolling without slipping on a stationary surface; conservation of mechanical energy separately requires no dissipative work.
rotational-kinetic-energy.units: K: J; M: kg; v_cm: m/s; I_cm: kg·m²; ω: rad/s; R: m

momentum-conservation.title: Momentum Balance and Conservation
momentum-conservation.plain: dP/dt = F_ext; if F_ext = 0, then P = const
momentum-conservation.meaning: The total momentum of a system is conserved when the net external force is zero.
momentum-conservation.conditions: The system must be closed with respect to momentum; internal forces are counted in pairs and do not change the total momentum.
momentum-conservation.units: P: kg·m/s; F: N; t: s

angular-momentum-balance.title: Angular Momentum Balance
angular-momentum-balance.plain: L_point = r × p; L_system = Σ_i r_i × p_i; dL/dt = τ_ext
angular-momentum-balance.meaning: A system's angular momentum is the sum of its particles' contributions, and external torque gives the rate of change of that sum.
angular-momentum-balance.conditions: All r_i and torques are measured about the same origin, fixed in an inertial frame; when the external torque is zero, the system's total L is conserved.
angular-momentum-balance.units: L: kg·m²/s; τ: N·m; r: m; p: kg·m/s

newton-gravitation.title: Newton's Law of Universal Gravitation
newton-gravitation.meaning: Two point masses attract each other with a force that decreases with the square of the distance between them.
newton-gravitation.conditions: The bodies are pointlike or spherically symmetric and do not overlap; this is the force on mass 1 due to mass 2; the field is Newtonian and weak.
newton-gravitation.units: F: N; G: m³/(kg·s²); m: kg; r: m

kepler-third-law.title: Kepler's Third Law for the Two-Body Problem
kepler-third-law.meaning: Relates the period of an elliptical relative orbit to its semimajor axis and the sum of the bodies' masses.
kepler-third-law.conditions: An isolated Newtonian two-body system of pointlike or spherically symmetric bodies; a is the semimajor axis of one body's orbit relative to the other; perturbations and relativistic corrections are small.
kepler-third-law.units: T: s; a: m; M and m: kg; G: m³/(kg·s²)

vis-viva-orbital-energy.title: Orbital Energy and the Vis-Viva Equation
vis-viva-orbital-energy.meaning: Relates specific relative-motion energy, speed, and position on a Keplerian orbit to the semimajor axis of its conic section.
vis-viva-orbital-energy.conditions: An isolated Newtonian two-body system of pointlike or nonoverlapping spherically symmetric bodies; r and v are relative separation and speed, and ε is energy per unit reduced mass. For an ellipse a > 0, for a parabola a tends to infinity, and for a hyperbola the convention a < 0 is used; drag, perturbations, and relativistic corrections are small.
vis-viva-orbital-energy.units: ε: J/kg = m²/s²; v: m/s; μ: m³/s²; r and a: m; M and m: kg
